newsitem.title: JORDAN: Japan grants Jordan $11.3 million for water scheme.
newsitem.headline: Japan grants Jordan $11.3 million for water scheme.

text.p: Japan granted Jordan on Tuesday $11.3 million to help the kingdom fully utilise extra water supplies it secured under a 1994 peace treaty with Israel, the Japanese embassy said.
The Japanese embassy in Amman said the grant will be used to replace water pumps in four pumping stations along the Jordan Valley to Amman to help boost water supplies to the capital.
"This project is regarded as part of the Japanese contribution in sustaining regional peace," an embassy statement said.
The water supplies will come from 45 million cubic metres of stored water from the Yarmouk river in Israel that is transported by pipeline to the King Abdullah Canal.
Japan has provided Jordan over $21.6 million of grants this year alone, the embassy said.
